title: What It Actually Looks Like to Chase Excellence Without Chasing Applause
caption:
Excellence and applause aren't the same appetite.

Notice which one you actually wanted. After the project ships, are you proud of the work, or relieved someone finally saw it?

Do the part no one will ever check. The email nobody rereads. The prep before the meeting nobody saw. That's where the real excellence lives, in the parts with no audience.

Let the credit go to someone else this week, on purpose. Not the humble-brag kind. Actual practice wanting the work right more than wanting your name on it.

"Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for the Lord." (Colossians 3:23)

The applause was never the point. It just felt like it.
